main_body: Thatched hut: a large pitched thatch roof (rows 0-36) over a plank-wall front with a central door and a side window (rows 37-63)
top_band: The thatch roof slope reads as the top surface, rows 1-34 in golden tones (L 126-214) with lighter courses. A lighter eave line sits at rows 34-35, then a dark eave shadow at rows 36-38.
evidence: The roof is a big foreshortened slope in thatch courses, ending in a bright eave edge with a dark shadow under it. Below that is the wall front with its own darker plank tones. The door has dark framing and iron straps, and the window is inset with a shutter. This matches how the Beodeul reference houses show a roof slope over a wall, so the building reads as 3/4.

style.evidence: The thatch has 5-6 lightness steps and per-course highlights, and flat-fill coverage is 0%. Median colours per tile is 10, close to the 11 and 18 of the references. The candidate has only 29 distinct colours against 66 and 185. The outline is the main weakness: 78% of dark edge pixels are neutral, against 7-9% in the references. The silhouette is wrapped in a black sticker-like line, where Beodeul uses dark material tones. This fails the outline craft standard.
